claim: 294 contaminated sites are mapped across Bangladesh using Pure Earth and University of Dhaka assessment data, across 93 upazilas in all divisions.
notes: Upazila count corrected to 93 in correction C-005; the earlier headline figure of 507 was wrong.
sources: Pure Earth Contaminated Sites Index (2016-2019) and University of Dhaka assessment data, as published in the live report

claim: 145 school–site intersections place schools within 500 metres of contaminated sites, for the 44 formally assessed headline sites. The unique-school count for those sites is 121, and the unique-student estimate is about 33,275.
notes: 145 counts intersections, not unique schools. Re-running against the archived snapshot gives 51 sites, 166 intersections, and 125 unique schools across all 294 sites; both counts are documented in the report.
sources: Live report and methodology: Haversine analysis, 500 metre screening threshold, OpenStreetMap schools snapshot March 2026

claim: The highest soil lead reading in the report reaches 680,872 ppm at Kathgora, Savar, about 1,702 times the 400 ppm international residential safety threshold.
sources: Live report, featured site BD-4921, Kathgora, Savar

claim: Zero contaminated sites have been permanently remediated or cleaned up, on the public record at the coordinates analysed.
notes: Enforcement closures and demolitions are not remediation. The claim is scoped to the public record at analysed coordinates.
sources: Live report, Reckoning section: no public record of permanent environmental soil remediation at any analysed coordinate

claim: About 39,875 exposure instances are projected (145 intersections x 275 average enrolment), with a unique-school estimate of about 33,275 and an audited range of 24,650 to 50,750.
notes: This is a projection from an enrolment model, not a count of tested children. It must not be quoted as children poisoned.
sources: Live report, March 2026 analysis; enrolment average 275 students per school, Annual Primary School Census 2024 / Directorate of Primary Education

claim: In UNICEF and Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics MICS 2025, 38.3% of children nationally and 65.2% in Dhaka Division exceed safe blood-lead limits, with Rajshahi lowest at 15.9%.
notes: Divisional rates are population survey rates, not clinical cohort rates.
sources: UNICEF / Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics MICS 2025, divisional data Table TC.S5 p.98, as published in the live report

claim: Only six formal, licensed recyclers operate in Bangladesh, processing about 30 percent of battery waste, while more than 6,000 informal workshops process about 70 percent.
notes: Informal count is given as 6,000 or more in the live report.
sources: Live report, formal versus informal section

claim: 68 sites are designated critical zones, with 65 exceeding 100,000 ppm (250 times safe).
notes: 68 and 65 are different numbers and must not be merged.
sources: Live report, critical areas section, as reconciled in correction C-005
